name: Cádiz
title: Cádiz Drydock UTM | Ship Thickness Measurement & Gauging
description: Ship thickness measurement in Cádiz Bay drydocks: renewal survey gauging, hull structure UTM and scrubber piping checks for ships docking in the bay.
h1: Thickness Gauging for Ships in the Cádiz Bay Drydocks
intro: The Bay of Cádiz is one of the main ship-repair centres of southern Spain, with Navantia's ship-repair yard at Cádiz docking cruise ships, gas carriers, tankers and other large merchant ships. A ship docking here for its renewal survey needs thickness gauging that does not hold up the yard. Technicians are mobilised from India to Cádiz for pre-docking surveys, in-dock measurement and post-blast confirmation, timed to the docking date the owner has fixed months in advance.

highlights.p: Dockings in the bay run to tight critical paths. We schedule pre-docking, in-dock and post-blast readings so steel lists reach the yard and the surveyor before the work reaches each area of the ship.

highlights.h: Cruise ship and gas carrier tanks
highlights.p: Large tank and void systems on cruise ships, and ballast and double-bottom structure on gas carriers, are measured by priority so the most important readings come first in a short docking.

highlights.h: Last dock before the Med ECA
highlights.p: Ships leaving Cádiz eastbound are inside the Mediterranean ECA soon after sailing. A docking here is the right moment to gauge and replace scrubber wash-water and overboard piping from outside the hull.

port.h: Cádiz Bay: drydocks at the Atlantic entrance to the Mediterranean
p: Cádiz's place in ship inspection comes from its drydocks rather than its cargo. Navantia's ship-repair yard in Cádiz is a long-established large-ship repair yard, and owners of cruise ships, gas carriers, tankers and large bulk carriers schedule dockings there, with Navantia's other sites around the bay adding shipbuilding and offshore fabrication. The Autoridad Portuaria de la Bahía de Cádiz handles a mixed but smaller cargo trade across Cádiz, El Puerto de Santa María, Puerto Real and the Zona Franca, along with cruise calls for visitors heading to Cádiz, Jerez and Seville, and a ro-pax link to the Canary Islands.

The yard's location is part of its appeal. Cádiz lies on the Atlantic coast just west of the Strait of Gibraltar, close to the main routes between the Atlantic, the Mediterranean and Suez, so a ship can divert for a docking with little deviation from its trade. Cruise lines use the bay for dockings between seasons, and gas carrier operators value a yard used to their ship types. Ships arriving for the yard often come straight from passage, so the first gauging may take place at anchor in the bay or alongside the repair quay before the ship enters the dock.

For gauging, this means planned, full-scope work. A renewal survey docking on a tanker, gas carrier or bulk carrier needs the thickness measurement programme set by the IACS unified requirements — extensive at the third renewal survey and later for ESP ships — and the yard's critical path depends on measurements arriving early. Cruise ships bring a different problem: extensive tank and void networks, tight docking periods and many contractors on board at once. In both cases, gauging before the ship arrives, or in the first days of the docking, lets steel renewal be ordered and planned before the yard reaches the areas concerned, which is where most of the value of drydock thickness gauging lies.

facilities.h: Drydock gauging around the Bay of Cádiz
p: Most gauging in the bay is done inside Navantia's Cádiz ship-repair yard, either at the repair quays before and after docking or in the dock itself. In the dock, the bottom and side shell can be measured from outside, the yard's gas-free certification and ventilation regime governs tank entry, and staging or lifts give access to high structure in holds and tanks. The yard's planning sets when each space is open, so the gauging programme is tied to the yard schedule and updated daily with the ship's superintendent.

Two rounds of measurement are common. The first, before or at the start of the docking, gives the surveyor and the yard the corrosion picture and the steel list; the second, after cleaning, blasting or cropping, confirms the thickness of areas left in place and the extent of renewal. For cruise ships, the volume of tanks and voids means the technicians often work in parallel with tank cleaners and painters, which needs close coordination with the yard's permit system. Ships waiting for a dock slot at anchor in the bay can be gauged by launch beforehand, which shortens the time the ship spends in the dock itself.
list: Navantia's Cádiz ship-repair yard — in-dock gauging of bottom shell, tanks, holds and decks for renewal and docking surveys on large merchant ships
Repair quays at the yard — pre-docking and post-undocking gauging alongside, including ballast tanks, piping and deck structure
Cádiz Bay anchorage — pre-docking gauging by launch on ships waiting for a dock slot, so the steel list is started early
Cruise berths in the port of Cádiz — short sea-water line and cofferdam checks on cruise ships making day calls, planned with the technical department
Port terminals at Cádiz and the Zona Franca — gauging on bulk carriers, ro-ro and container ships calling for cargo
Gibraltar and Algeciras — nearby ports where gauging can begin on passage before a ship continues to a docking in the bay

context.h: Regulation and market context for Cádiz dockings
p: Cádiz lies on the Atlantic side of the Mediterranean SOx ECA boundary, so ships docking here are outside the ECA but enter it within hours of sailing east. That makes a Cádiz docking a natural moment to inspect scrubber systems before a Mediterranean season: wash-water and overboard lines, their discharge valves and the adjoining shell plating can be gauged and renewed in the dock, where access from outside is easy. Port state control in the port follows the Paris MoU, applied by the Spanish maritime administration through its local harbour master.

Cruise ships and gas carriers are among the ship types most associated with the yard, and both have particular gauging needs. Cruise ships run large ballast, fresh water, grey and black water tank systems that are only fully accessible in dock, and their docking periods are short and tightly scheduled. Gas carriers' hull and ballast tank structure is surveyed under the class rules for their type, while their cargo containment is a separate specialist matter outside ultrasonic gauging. Since EU ETS reached shipping in 2024 and FuelEU Maritime followed in 2025, more dockings also include energy-saving retrofits, which open structure that needs measuring before it is modified.

jobs.p: Work in Cádiz is usually tied to a fixed docking date set well in advance, which suits technicians travelling from India: visas, the measurement plan and the steel estimate can all be prepared before the ship arrives. Typical jobs combine pre-docking readings with in-dock and post-blast measurement, sized to the survey and the ship type. Larger dockings may need the team to stay for most of the yard period.
list: Third renewal survey gauging on a Suezmax tanker docked at the Cádiz yard: cargo and ballast tank structure, bottom and deck plating to the ESP extent, delivered in phases to keep the yard on schedule.
Cruise ship docking between seasons: ballast, fresh water and grey water tank gauging, sea chest and shell readings from outside, and scrubber overboard pipe measurement in dock.
Pre-docking gauging of an LNG carrier's ballast tanks and double bottom at anchor in the bay, so that steel renewal is estimated before the ship enters the dock.
Post-blast thickness readings on a bulk carrier's hopper tanks and hold frames, confirming which areas the surveyor accepts and which must be cropped and renewed.
Aft peak tank, rudder trunk and stern frame area gauging before the yard fits an energy-saving duct or a new propeller, so the structure around the work is confirmed sound.

logistics: Technicians fly from India to Jerez or Seville, usually via Madrid or another European hub, and reach Cádiz by road; Málaga and Gibraltar are alternatives. Yard access is arranged through the shipyard and the ship's superintendent, with induction and safety passes issued at the gate, while anchorage work is arranged by the ship's agent with a launch. Schengen visas are needed, and since dockings in the bay are typically booked months ahead, we align visa applications with the docking date and the yard's planning meetings.

faqs.q: When should gauging start for a renewal survey docking in Cádiz?
faqs.a: Ideally before the ship arrives. Pre-docking readings at anchor or at a previous port give the yard a steel estimate to plan against, and the first days in dock are then spent on areas only accessible there — bottom shell, gas-freed cargo tanks, high structure on staging. Leaving all gauging to the docking risks steel orders arriving late on the yard's critical path.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a cruise ship's tanks during a short Cádiz docking?
faqs.a: Yes, with planning. Cruise ship tank networks are extensive, so we agree priorities with the technical superintendent — usually tanks due for survey, known problem areas and those adjoining shell renewals — and work alongside the yard's cleaning and painting crews. Readings are issued as each group of tanks is completed, so renewal decisions are taken before the ship floats out.

faqs.q: Is Cádiz inside the Mediterranean ECA?
faqs.a: No. The ECA boundary is a meridian in the Strait near Tarifa, east of Cádiz, so the bay is outside it. Ships leaving a Cádiz docking eastbound enter the ECA soon after sailing, and owners often use the docking to gauge and renew scrubber wash-water and overboard piping while it can be reached from outside the hull.

faqs.q: Do you work for the yard or directly for the owner?
faqs.a: Our contract is with the shipowner or manager, and we plan the gauging around the yard's programme in coordination with the superintendent and the yard's planners. The yard decides access, gas-freeing and staging; the attending class surveyor decides what readings are needed for the survey. We report to the owner in the form the survey requires, with copies to the yard where the owner agrees.
